correctness.rationale: The two-sided stationary SDE decomposes Y as U_a+√τG; stationary telegraph flux gives density of U_a proportional to (1−u²)^(a−1) on (−1,1), with independent Gaussian G. Central curvature is −F_a(z)/(τ√(2πτ)B(1/2,a)), z=1/(2τ), F=I+2zI′, I=B·1F1(1/2;a+1/2;−z). Kummer equation gives F′(z*)=(a−1)I(z*)/z*<0 at any root for a<1. F(0)>0 and large-z F<0, so exactly one downward crossing. Derivative of Gaussian-convolved beta density has at most 3 sign alternations by truncation and strict total positivity of the exponential/Laplace kernel; the local curvature sign therefore decides the global one-vs-two mode count. At criticality the heat equation plus transversality yields fourth derivative p4(0)<0. At a≥1 beta component unimodal, and convolution strictly unimodal. Weak limit a→0 is two point masses, yielding τc→1; limit a→1 is uniform, yielding τc→0. Independently checked three root values and sign identity (a=0.1,0.5,0.9) as finite confirmation.

final_claim: For stationary 1D symmetric harmonic RTP with switching ratio a=λ/κ, noise τ=Dκ/v²>0: if 0<a<1 there is exactly one hypergeometric root threshold τc(a), exactly two strict modes for τ<τc and one at/above (quartic-flat at threshold); a≥1 is strictly unimodal for all τ; τc→1 as a↓0 and →0 as a↑1.
limitations: One-dimensional symmetric two-state telegraph and harmonic confinement with additive independent Gaussian noise only.
The critical curve is implicit, no uniform extensions to unequal switching, interacting RTPs or 2D.
